evidence.summary: Braxton emerges from an artificial temporal rift, attacks Voyager while claiming it will cause a 29th-century solar-system disaster, and the ensuing conflict pulls both ships into the rift, leaving Voyager at Earth in 1996.
Voyager identifies the year as 1996 and detects anomalous subspace technology in Los Angeles that should not exist for roughly another century.
SETI astronomer Rain Robinson detects Voyager's gamma/subspace signature and reports it to Starling, who orders her evidence suppressed and later authorizes violence to contain exposure.

An older, homeless Braxton says he has been stranded since 1967, explains his causal-loop model, retracts his original belief that Voyager caused the disaster, and identifies his stolen timeship as the likely cause if Starling launches it without proper calibration.
Older Braxton says Starling found the Aeon after Braxton beamed out from its 1967 crash and has used future technology to build power and technological advantage.
Tuvok and Paris investigate Rain's detection, erase her stored evidence to reduce timeline contamination, and are attacked by Starling's agent.
Janeway and Chakotay infiltrate Chronowerx, discover a protected future-tech database, and coordinate copying evidence about Starling and the timeship.
Janeway tells Starling his proposed future flight risks a temporal explosion costing billions of lives and demands return of the Aeon; Starling refuses.

Starling uses 29th-century technology to disrupt Voyager's transporter/computer systems, steals part of its database, and abducts the Doctor's program as the crisis becomes publicly visible on 20th-century media.

object.to: Aeon misuse by Starling causes disaster

assertions.subject: voy-fe1:braxton_1996
counterevidence: The prediction is based on Braxton's reconstruction of future chronometric evidence and has not yet occurred in this work.

neutral_coding.plot_problem: A future officer's attempt to prevent a catastrophe strands Voyager in 1996, where a technology entrepreneur possesses the future timeship that may cause the event.
neutral_coding.epistemics: Braxton's initial accusation, later reconstructed causal hypothesis, measurable anachronistic technology, and Starling's actions remain distinct.
neutral_coding.identity_timeline: Young/attacking and older/stranded Braxton are separate local temporal states rather than silently merged.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: Braxton explicitly admits his first Voyager-causation theory was wrong, preserving the correction trail.
